nodes.label: core/db.py transaction
nodes.rationale: The repeated shape is open a connection, commit on success, rollback in except, and close in finally. routes/api/access.py close is the only shared closer. It is used by department, course, year, semester, batch, subject, allocation, and holiday saves and deletes, by room delete, and by branding init, update, and reset. The read after a year, batch, or holiday save stays outside the block. Student, faculty, account, shift, user, and room-save handlers still call commit() because some input-error paths do not roll back. Availability saves that commit a delete before the insert, and the timetable generator commits, were not wrapped. nodes.label: Availability and absence copies
nodes.rationale: Generation blocks on an absence that date, a busy span already assigned in the run, or an overlapping is_available 0 window. A recorded shift window does not block a slot outside that shift. Manual add is stricter: if any availability row exists for that faculty and day, the slot must sit inside an is_available 1 window. Availability saves in admin and faculty routes delete existing rows and insert the submitted slots. One path commits the delete before the insert. Teacher absence inserts use status UNPROCESSED and session faculty_id, which is faculty.id. Admin absence inserts use status PROCESSED and the faculty id in the URL.

nodes.label: Clash check copies
nodes.rationale: Python overlap is _times_overlap. SQL overlap uses NOT (end_time <= start OR start_time >= end). The predicate matches. The is_active filter does not. Manual timetable checks use COALESCE(is_active, 1) = 1. Proxy free checks do not filter is_active. A shared helper must take that filter as an argument supplied by the caller.

nodes.label: Date and time parsing copies
nodes.rationale: HH:MM, ISO dates, ISO datetimes with a trailing Z, clock display including MySQL timedelta, 12-hour display, and weekday names were copied across timetable, faculty, student, admin, and API routes. The four format_time copies match except routes/students/student.py, which returns a string unchanged. safe_clock wraps a timedelta with modulo 86400. Callers keep their own error text. Display formats other than HH:MM stay at the call site.

nodes.label: Holiday check copies
nodes.rationale: Generation loads recurring days and dates inside the week. The manual add form only rejects a recurring holiday for that weekday and program and does not look up a calendar date. Create and edit uniqueness reject a second recurring row; the API also excludes the row being edited and the HTML form does not. The dashboard upcoming list is read-only and is not a scheduling rule. Do not make the manual add use the week query.

nodes.label: Proxy assignment copies
nodes.rationale: find_and_assign_proxy inserts proxy_log with status only. _admin_find_and_assign_proxy inserts the same match and also sets approval_status APPROVED, approval_date, and approved_by. The free check under both is the same timetable overlap and does not filter is_active. Proxy inserts stay separate because the column lists differ.

nodes.label: Academic term
nodes.rationale: A term is a stretch of one academic year. kind is teaching, exam, break or internship. Dates are inclusive and must sit inside the academic year. A null semester means the whole year and overlaps every semester term. An exam, break or internship term wins over a teaching term on the same date. A date in no term is not a teaching day once the institution has any term.

An empty file is produced when the capability is off. faculty-workload adds norm columns only while workload_norms is on.

nodes.label: Exam seating and hall tickets
nodes.rationale: Exam seating plans and hall tickets use the same PDF renderer but are not queued report types. They download from the exam while capability exams is on.

nodes.label: CSV Excel and PDF renderers

PDF is landscape when there are more than seven columns. The download mimetype comes from the file extension.

nodes.label: Academic calendar, syllabus, assessments and exams
nodes.norm_label: academic calendar, syllabus, assessments and exams

nodes.label: academic_terms capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off, or before any term is saved, timetables, close-day and attendance behave exactly as they do today, so the calendar is an optional overlay rather than a change to the core.

nodes.label: assessments capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off there is no Internals entry, the student and teacher tabs stay hidden, and nothing is stored. External results, grades and transcripts are not computed here. Students see a mark only after the component is locked; unlocking hides it again. Attainment figures and the report count every entered mark, locked or not.

nodes.label: Exam seating and invigilation solver
nodes.rationale: Solving places every selected paper on one slot. Two papers that share a student never share a slot. A shared elective is one paper, so every cohort that selected it sits it together. Usable seats are room capacity divided by one more than the seating gap, then capped by students per room. Each used room gets one invigilator who is not absent, not unavailable, and not already on duty in that slot. Duties are spread so the busiest person has as few sessions as possible.

nodes.label: exams capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off there is no Exams entry and nothing is stored. Room bookings and the weekly generator are otherwise unchanged. While bookings is on, solved rooms are busy at that date and time, so a new booking is refused and the generator avoids them for that week. A weekly timetable slot is not blocked by a one-day exam. Regular classes during an exam term are cancelled by the academic calendar when that capability is on, with reason calendar.

nodes.label: Course and program outcome attainment
nodes.rationale: A component percentage is marks over maximum times 100. A course-outcome score is the weighted mean of the mapped component percentages; a weight of 0 on every mapped component counts them equally. Students with no mark on those components are left out. Attainment is the mean of the counted students. The level follows the share at or above 60 percent: 3 at 70 percent or more, 2 at 60, 1 at 50, otherwise 0. A program outcome is the mean of mapped course-outcome percentages weighted by correlation level 1 to 3, then the same bands.

nodes.label: syllabus capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off the mark screen has no topic field, a topic sent by the mobile app is ignored, and nothing is written to lesson_logs. syllabus_units is the plan for one subject; lesson_logs is one topic per held lecture, with hours from 0.5 to 3 defaulting to 1. An invalid topic rejects that event before the mark is stored.

nodes.label: Syllabus coverage pace
nodes.rationale: Coverage is delivered hours of held lectures divided by planned hours. When the academic calendar is configured, expected hours are planned times elapsed teaching weeks over total teaching weeks; a week counts once its Monday is today or earlier. More than half an hour above that is ahead, more than half an hour below is behind, otherwise on_track. With no calendar the pace is no_pace and the percentage is still shown. Attendance percentages are unchanged.

nodes.label: workload_norms capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. Off, limits and assessments are empty, so neither solver sees a norm, the workload_max rule costs nothing, and the workload report keeps its old columns. The norms live in timetable_rules under _workload, with no table of their own. enforce defaults to soft, a cost, rather than a hard constraint.

nodes.label: API keys and scopes
nodes.rationale: The plaintext key is shown once. Only the prefix and a SHA-256 hash are stored. A key carries the scopes it was created with and cannot gain one later; create another key instead. Scopes are catalog:read, timetable:read, people:read and attendance:read. catalog:read includes subject coverage only while syllabus is on and locked internal marks only while assessments is on. Per-key limit defaults to 600 a minute.

nodes.label: flask admin create-superadmin
nodes.rationale: The only way the first account is made, and it needs the Super Admin role that seed run inserts. The password is stored as a werkzeug hash. The audit entry never includes the password or hash. --force only adds another account; it never changes an existing one.

nodes.label: Permission canon
nodes.rationale: tests/unit/test_permission_canon.py scans every permission check and fails if the code checks a name that is not in the canon, if a permission marked enforced is not checked anywhere, or if a permission marked not enforced is outside its allowlist of 24.

nodes.label: Unenforced permissions
nodes.rationale: 24 permissions that no code checks still exist on installed databases and are shown in the role editor, where granting or removing them does nothing. Do not delete the rows. Either add the check or hide them, then change enforced and update the allowlist.

nodes.label: Institution memberships
nodes.rationale: A user may belong to several institutions with different roles. users.role and users.department_id stay the primary identity. The 0014 backfill puts every non-student into institution 1, and a new teacher joins the institution of their department. Other memberships are added with SQL for now; the user editor has no Institutions field yet. The last active institution cannot be deactivated.

nodes.label: Institution follow-ups
nodes.rationale: Not in revision 0014: per-institution overrides of calendar, attendance policy, branding and notifications; cross-institution student enrolment; an organization dashboard; sharing of lab batch groups or subjects; and scoping of reports, accreditation exports, invitations, the user list and the public API.

nodes.label: Face templates
nodes.rationale: Recognition runs on the device. The server stores one 192-float template per person and pushes it to devices. The server never receives camera frames for recognition; it receives the device's verdict: confidence and optionally liveness score and frame hash.

nodes.label: Report export queue
nodes.rationale: POST /api/reports queues the job. services/export_jobs.py writes the file. GET /api/reports/id/download returns it. The users, audit-log and timetable bulk exports stream row by row and stay CSV; they are not this queue.

nodes.label: First install
nodes.rationale: install.sh sets up packages, the virtualenv, the frontend build, systemd and nginx. One college then runs flask db upgrade, flask seed run and flask admin create-superadmin. Several colleges use flask tenant init and flask tenant create. TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT is 1 for nginx. REQUIRE_MIGRATED_DB and REQUIRE_WORKERS make /health return 503 until the schema is at head and the worker heartbeat is fresh.

nodes.label: VPS process layout
nodes.rationale: timetable-web.service runs gunicorn on port 8000 with BACKGROUND_WORKERS false. timetable-workers.service runs flask workers run: the export queue, the timetable queue, the nightly close-day and the quality-model retrainer. A systemd timer runs deploy/backup.sh nightly. Everything lives under /opt/timetable, owned by the timetable user. Two worker hosts are safe because claims carry locked_by.

nodes.label: Reports and exports
nodes.rationale: Every report is queued from the Reports page, written by the export worker, and downloaded by id. The note covers file formats and the NAAC/NBA accreditation templates.

nodes.label: Account authority
nodes.rationale: roles.hierarchy_level orders roles; smaller is more senior. An actor manages only accounts whose role level is larger than their own, and can only give a role they could manage. Only a Super Admin manages a Super Admin, and the last active Super Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. Nobody deactivates their own account. Granting or revoking a user's permissions needs users_manage_permissions, held by no role but Super Admin by default, and only permissions the actor holds. Checks read the actor's role from the database and apply to the JSON API and the legacy admin routes.

nodes.label: Sign-in rate limits
nodes.rationale: Counters live in rate_limit_counters. Behind a reverse proxy, TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT must equal the real number of proxies so ProxyFix reads the client from X-Forwarded-For. It is 0 by default, and then the headers are ignored. Never set it higher than the real number of proxies: a client could then choose its own address.

nodes.label: flask seed run
nodes.rationale: Seeders only add rows. They never update or delete one, so a role, permission or branding value a college has changed stays. Role-permission defaults are one-time grants recorded in seed_history, so a permission a college removed stays removed. An existing database that already has role permissions is not granted the rest until flask seed run --apply-role-defaults. A later default carries a higher since version and is granted once. Super Admin passes every permission check whatever its rows say; it is mapped to every permission only so the role editor shows it complete. There are no default accounts or passwords.

nodes.label: Time-based sign-in lock
nodes.rationale: Five failures within fifteen minutes set locked_until fifteen minutes ahead by the database clock. The lock ends by itself. Every failed sign-in form POST answers the same 401 whether the username is unknown, the password is wrong, or the account is locked or inactive, and an unknown username still runs one password hash. status locked remains a manual lock, but sign-in no longer sets it. Rows locked that way before 0006 stay locked until an admin unlocks them. Super Admin accounts get the same temporary lock.

nodes.label: Request scope
nodes.rationale: core/scope.py resolves a Scope per request. Super Admin is organization-wide. Everyone else sees their memberships. Reads of a row outside the scope answer not found, so the id is not confirmed. Writes on a shared row the caller can see but does not own answer 403. The scope is in addition to permissions. The session stores only the chosen institution_id; the visible list is read on each request, so a membership change applies without a new sign-in.

nodes.label: One-college short-circuit
nodes.rationale: While the tenant has at most one active institution, multiple is false, every predicate is 1=1 and allows is always true, so a one-college install runs exactly the pre-0014 queries. A staff user with no membership is placed in the institution of their department, else the first institution. The switcher, institution field and sharing controls appear only when more than one institution is active.

nodes.label: Face template encryption
nodes.rationale: Templates are encrypted with Fernet under FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY. The key lives in the environment, never in the database or the repository, so a database dump alone does not expose biometric data. Reads accept legacy plaintext; writes always encrypt when a key is set. Do not run production without a key. /health reports the key as configured or missing but does not return 503, because an installation without face attendance has no key. Rotation uses FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY_PREVIOUS and flask face rotate-key for every tenant.

nodes.label: OpenID Connect staff sign-in
nodes.rationale: Admins, HODs and teachers can sign in with Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID or any OpenID Connect provider. Students keep the password form because their accounts have no verified staff email. The flow is authorization code with PKCE. The id token must be RS256 and is checked for issuer, audience, expiry, issued-at, not-before, nonce and subject. Link-by-email matches exactly one non-student account on a verified email inside the allowed domains. Locked or inactive accounts are refused as they are for passwords.

nodes.label: Secrets rotation
nodes.rationale: Changing SECRET_KEY signs everyone out. MYSQL_PASSWORD must also change in MariaDB. MOBILE_SYNC_API_KEY forces devices to re-register. FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY rotation sets the new key, keeps the old one in FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY_PREVIOUS, restarts, runs flask face rotate-key for every tenant, then removes the previous key.

nodes.label: Open lab-batch audit xfail
nodes.rationale: test_audit_regressions.py treats as still open the bug that a practical cannot be limited to a lab batch because there are no lab sub-batch tables, and points at DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md. That design says revision 0012 implemented the tables.

nodes.label: 0009_worker_claims
nodes.rationale: Adds locked_by and heartbeat_at to processed_reports and timetable_jobs so a restart or a second worker requeues only rows whose heartbeat is older than JOB_STALE_SECONDS.

nodes.label: 0010_face_safeguards
nodes.rationale: Creates face_consents and face_recognition_audit. Face templates themselves are encrypted in place by the application; this revision changes no template columns.

nodes.label: 0011_notifications
nodes.rationale: Creates the notifications outbox and the single-row notification_settings table, including a Fernet-encrypted SMTP password and the shared claim columns.

nodes.label: 0012_lab_batches
nodes.rationale: Creates lab_batch_groups and lab_batch_members and adds nullable timetable.lab_batch_group_id. Null means a whole-division slot. The foreign key is ON DELETE SET NULL.

nodes.label: 0013_integrations
nodes.rationale: Creates api_keys, webhook_endpoints, webhook_deliveries, sso_settings and sso_identities. Webhook secrets and the SSO client secret are Fernet-encrypted.

nodes.label: 0014_institutions
nodes.rationale: Several colleges in one tenant. Backfill inserts organization and institution 1 before the foreign keys, leaves existing departments and rooms there, and gives every non-student user a primary membership. Downgrade drops the columns and tables, so which college owned what is lost. The DEFAULT 1 is deliberate so inserts that do not name an institution still land in the first one.

nodes.label: Institutions
nodes.rationale: Implemented in revision 0014. A tenant was one college. A university that shares a few labs and a visiting professor needs a level inside the tenant, because a separate tenant cannot share a room or a person.

nodes.label: Lab batches
nodes.rationale: Implemented in revision 0012. Describes what exists; the original gap and the choices made are kept for context.

nodes.label: Face attendance safeguards
nodes.rationale: How face data is stored, who may be enrolled, how a device's recognitions are checked before they become attendance, and how a device is tied to the lecture the teacher opened.

nodes.label: Integrations
nodes.rationale: Public API, webhooks and staff single sign-on, configured on Settings, Integrations.

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.rationale: Email alerts for a student below the attendance threshold, a cancelled lecture, a substitute, lectures nobody marked, and shift-change requests.

nodes.label: Timetable Management documentation
nodes.rationale: These notes describe the application as it runs now: a React screen on port 5173 and a Flask API on port 5000. The browser uses the React routes and /api; route_inventory.md is an older generated URL list whose legacy views may still exist.

nodes.label: route_inventory.md
nodes.rationale: An older generated list of Flask URLs. Some of those paths still exist as legacy views.

nodes.label: TENANCY.md
nodes.rationale: Serving several colleges from one installation: the tenant registry, flask tenant, routing by hostname, and per-tenant workers and files. A tenant is the isolation boundary and who you sell to.

nodes.label: Production runbook
nodes.rationale: One Linux VPS per environment. nginx proxies to gunicorn, which talks to MariaDB 10.4. Workers, backups and the web process are separate services so a schema change can stop job claims without stopping the admin path entirely.

nodes.label: Tenant connection settings
nodes.rationale: models.db.connection_settings() opens the bound tenant database for rate limits, session lookup, the view, and the branding context processor. With a registry and no bound tenant it raises rather than falling back to MYSQL_DB.

nodes.label: Tenancy live tests
nodes.rationale: tests/integration/test_tenancy_live.py needs --live-db. It builds college_timetable_ci_tenant_{registry,alpha,beta}_test, provisions two colleges, and checks migrations, seed rows, hostname routing, cross-host session anonymity, tenant upgrade --all, the close-day worker, unbound get_db_connection, and tenant forget keeping the database. config.testing.test_database_problem applies to the registry name and every bound db_name. All three databases are dropped at the end.

nodes.label: Tenant registry schema
nodes.rationale: core/tenancy/registry.py SCHEMA is the definition. The registry is not under Alembic. flask tenant init, or the first tenant create, creates the table.

nodes.label: Tenant request routing
nodes.rationale: core/tenancy/request.py is the first before_request hook. It lower-cases the Host header, drops the port, and asks the registry. On a match it binds the tenant to g.tenant. /health and /static/ do not need a tenant.

nodes.label: flask tenant commands
nodes.rationale: Commands are init, create, list, upgrade (one slug or --all), set-status, and forget. Other commands need --tenant SLUG when a registry is configured, including seed run, admin create-superadmin, attendance, and db-adopt.

nodes.label: Tenancy unit tests
nodes.rationale: tests/unit/test_tenancy.py covers hostname parsing, validation, the lookup cache, session binding, path scoping, and the refusals. bind and create_app refuse a real database name in a testing app, and --tenant without a registry is refused.

nodes.label: Tenant health check
nodes.rationale: With a registry, /health checks that the registry answers and that every active tenant database is at the head revision when REQUIRE_MIGRATED_DB is on. The first problem is reported as Tenant <slug>: .... A healthy response includes tenancy registry.

nodes.label: Tenant mobile devices
nodes.rationale: Devices authenticate against mobile_devices in the tenant database they reach by hostname, so a device registered with one college cannot sync to another even with a valid signature.

nodes.label: Single college mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode. MYSQL_DB names the database and TENANT_REGISTRY_DB is unset, so every request uses that database. Existing single-college installations change nothing. Migrations stay flask db upgrade.

nodes.label: Tenant
nodes.rationale: A tenant is the outer boundary: nothing is shared across it. Each tenant has its own MariaDB database. Nothing in that database refers to another tenant.

nodes.label: Tenant hostname cache
nodes.rationale: Hostname lookups are cached in the process for TENANT_CACHE_SECONDS, default 30, so a status change takes effect within that time on every worker.

nodes.label: Tenant registry
nodes.rationale: TENANT_REGISTRY_DB names a database on the same server, reached with MYSQL_HOST, MYSQL_USER, and MYSQL_PASSWORD. The Host header selects the tenant. An unknown host returns 404 and a suspended tenant returns 503. flask db is not registered; upgrades are flask tenant upgrade.

nodes.label: tenants table
nodes.rationale: Columns id, slug, hostname, db_name, status, created_at, updated_at. slug, hostname, and db_name are each unique. status is provisioning, active, or suspended.

nodes.label: Tenancy
nodes.rationale: One installation can serve several colleges. Each college is a tenant with its own database, reached at its own hostname.

nodes.label: Database boundary isolation
nodes.rationale: Isolation is the database boundary, not a tenant_id column. A tenant database never refers to another tenant.

nodes.label: Tenant session binding
nodes.rationale: A signed-in session stores the slug it was opened on in session['tenant'], written by an after_request hook on the sign-in response. A cookie presented on another college's hostname is cleared before anything reads it. Set SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN only with the understanding that this binding, not the cookie scope, keeps sessions apart.

nodes.label: Tenant provisioning
nodes.rationale: tenant create registers the slug as provisioning, creates the database with utf8mb4_unicode_ci, runs every migration and the seeders, creates the Super Admin when admin username and email are given, then marks the tenant active. It refuses a slug, hostname, or database name already in use, and refuses a database that already exists. The default database name is college_timetable_<slug> with hyphens turned into underscores. If a step fails the tenant stays provisioning: forget the slug, drop the database by hand if it was created, and run create again.

nodes.label: Tenant forget
nodes.rationale: tenant forget removes the registry row only. The app never drops a tenant database.

nodes.label: Per-tenant workers
nodes.rationale: The close-day worker, the export queue, the timetable queue, and the quality-model retrainer call core.tenancy.tenants_to_serve(app) and run once per active tenant inside tenant_context. A tenant that fails is logged and the others continue. A tenant added while the app is running is picked up on the next pass.

nodes.label: college_timetable.sql
nodes.rationale: Was sql/college_timetable.sql. Early scratch schema. It defines some tables twice, has a broken users insert, stores plaintext passwords, and runs truncate rooms. It does not match the current schema.

nodes.label: 2026-03-30 data dump
nodes.rationale: college_timetable_db_20260330_231208.sql was in migrations/. It contains real user rows and password hashes, so it stays out of git because *.sql is ignored. Local copy only.

nodes.label: hash_passwords.py
nodes.rationale: Was in scripts/. One-off script that hashed plaintext passwords in users. It imports mysql from app, which no longer exists, so it does not run as written. The updated command is python -m legacy.hash_passwords.

nodes.label: run_full_migration
nodes.rationale: Was in scripts/. Drops and recreates every table in the .env database from backups/college_timetable_db_2026_03_30.sql, then reloads the data. It rewrites collations and some column definitions. Replaced by Alembic revisions. Run as python legacy/run_full_migration.py or legacy\run_full_migration.bat.

nodes.label: migrations/_archive
nodes.rationale: _archive/ holds the first baseline attempt and is not part of the chain.

nodes.label: migrations/sql baseline
nodes.rationale: The baseline SQL and its schema snapshot live in sql/.

nodes.label: migrations/versions
nodes.rationale: Hand-written Alembic revisions live in versions/.

nodes.label: Alembic revisions
nodes.rationale: Schema changes are hand-written Alembic revisions. flask db migrate autogenerate is disabled.

nodes.label: Legacy scripts
nodes.rationale: Files kept for reference only. Nothing in the application, the tests, or the Alembic setup imports or runs them.

nodes.label: docs/DATABASE.md
nodes.rationale: Read docs/DATABASE.md before adding a revision or touching an existing database.

nodes.label: Migrations
nodes.rationale: Hand-written Alembic revisions. Read docs/DATABASE.md before adding a revision or touching an existing database.

nodes.label: Legacy reference-only rule
nodes.rationale: Do not run these files against a database you need to keep. They were moved here before database migrations were introduced, so the only schema path left in the main tree is migrations/. Both runnable scripts read the database from .env. Back up the database first.

nodes.label: Adopt an existing database
nodes.rationale: An existing database uses flask db-adopt --check, then flask db-adopt. Do not run flask db stamp or flask db upgrade on it by hand.

nodes.label: Empty database upgrade
nodes.rationale: A new, empty database is brought up with flask db upgrade.

nodes.label: Immutable revisions
nodes.rationale: Never edit a revision after a database has been upgraded or stamped with it, and always write downgrade().

nodes.label: Autogenerate disabled
nodes.rationale: flask db migrate (autogenerate) is disabled so revisions stay hand-written.

nodes.label: 0001_baseline
nodes.rationale: Creates college_timetable_db: 54 tables and 10 views. migrations/_archive kept a first attempt that reused the revision id 0001_baseline, so a database stamped by that old attempt would look adopted when it is not. college_timetable_db was adopted and upgraded to 0007 on 8 Nov 2026; 0008 had not been applied yet.

nodes.label: flask db-adopt
nodes.rationale: An existing database already has the baseline tables, so flask db upgrade from nothing would fail. db-adopt compares information_schema to the baseline snapshot inside a read-only transaction and, if nothing differs and the database is unstamped, stamps 0001_baseline and nothing else. Do not edit the baseline to make a database fit. Check alembic_version before adopting, because the archived baseline reused that revision id.

nodes.label: MariaDB 10.4.32
nodes.rationale: 10.4.32-MariaDB is the supported engine. The baseline, its snapshot and the tests are taken on that version. Other MariaDB or MySQL versions report types, defaults and view text differently, so flask db-adopt will warn about differences that come only from the server. The MySQL 8.2 dumps in backups are not the schema source: they use utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, which MariaDB 10.4 does not have. Regenerate the baseline with the XAMPP MariaDB mysqldump, not the MySQL client on PATH, because phpMyAdmin drops CHECK constraints.

nodes.label: 0008_attendance_views
nodes.rationale: Makes attendance.session_id NOT NULL and drops attendance_summary and student_overall_attendance, which no code reads. It refuses to run while any attendance row has no session_id. Downgrade makes the column nullable again and recreates the views from the baseline text.

nodes.label: Startup schema check
nodes.rationale: When REQUIRE_MIGRATED_DB is true, startup compares alembic_version with the newest revision. If the database is behind, unstamped, unknown or unreachable, /health returns 503. Other routes are not blocked. /health checks again on every call, so it returns 200 as soon as the database is upgraded, without a restart. Flask CLI commands other than flask run start no background work and skip this check.

nodes.label: Attendance calculation phases
nodes.rationale: Each phase ships and is tested on its own so the suite stays green between phases. Phase 0 is the pure module. Phase 1 records sessions. Phase 2 moves student and defaulter screens. Phase 3 moves reports, the mobile roster and the absent fill. Phase 4 makes session_id NOT NULL and drops both views. Phase 1 as shipped left the mobile permission check unchanged; phase 3 closed it. On 9 Nov 2026 college_timetable_db was at 0007 with every mark linked, and 0008 had not been applied.

nodes.label: Attendance calculation foundation
nodes.rationale: Approved 8 Nov 2026 with the recommended default for every open question. Phases 0 through 4 are described as shipped. Phase 5 was not started in this design. Live-database facts came from read-only counts on 8 Nov 2026.

nodes.label: Alembic schema ownership
nodes.rationale: Alembic, through Flask-Migrate, owns the schema. The application still reads and writes rows with raw SQL in models/db.py and has no ORM models, so autogenerate is disabled: it would only propose dropping every table. The app never runs DDL itself. Never edit a revision once any database has been upgraded or stamped with it. Always write downgrade. Test a new revision on a copy before college_timetable_db. Hand-written revisions only.

nodes.label: flask attendance backfill-sessions
nodes.rationale: Creates one held session with source backfill for every timetable and date that has attendance rows but no session, and links those rows. It never invents unmarked lectures. It only reports anomalies. Marks on a cancelled session stay unlinked until they are deleted or the session is restored. It is the one command that runs on a database at 0007 or later; every other command needs head. The deployment order when 0008 stops is upgrade, backfill, upgrade.

nodes.label: Mixed collations
nodes.rationale: academic_terms and timetable_jobs use utf8mb4_general_ci; the other 52 baseline tables use utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Left as is because changing a collation can break joins and comparisons. A later fix belongs in its own revision, tested on a copy.

nodes.label: Historical session backfill
nodes.rationale: Backfill creates held sessions only for dates that already have marks. It never creates not_marked rows for the past, because nothing records which past lectures were held, so percentages before phase 1 use marked lectures only. Anomalies, including the 10 Feb 2026 weekday mismatch, are reported and still linked. The recommended treatment of those four live rows is to backfill them as held, because that is what was marked.

nodes.label: Legacy attendance views
nodes.rationale: Six independent computations none of which know whether a lecture was held. attendance_summary counts weekly slots, so the percentage exceeds 100 percent after the first week, and a null division never matches. student_overall_attendance counts distinct slots that have any row, so repeated marks exceed 100 percent and a skipped student leaves the denominator. The admin defaulter export selected column names the view does not have and returned 500. Both views are dropped in 0008 because a rebuilt view would freeze one policy into SQL that every consumer shares blindly.

nodes.label: Backup and restore drill
nodes.rationale: Nightly backup writes one gzipped dump per database, a tar of uploads, and SHA256SUMS. Restore into a new database name rather than overwriting. MariaDB RENAME is not available across databases, so either point the tenant registry at the restored name or restore with replace after stopping both services. The drill compares counts of users, attendance and lecture_sessions. Repeat it after every MariaDB upgrade. The face template key stays in .env only, out of the database backups.

nodes.label: Upgrade and rollback
nodes.rationale: Stop the workers so nothing claims jobs while the schema changes, and take a dump before any schema change. If db upgrade stops at 0008 because attendance rows have no session_id, backfill, resolve marks on a cancelled lecture, then upgrade again. Rollback is flask db downgrade or a restore of the pre-upgrade dump, then the previous git tag. Revisions are written so a downgrade removes only what the upgrade added.

nodes.label: flask attendance close-day
nodes.rationale: For each active slot that meets that weekday, close-day inserts not_marked unless a session already exists, the date is a holiday, or the date is outside the slot's semester. It refuses today and future dates. It also completes the roster of held sessions a face device recorded: each roster student without a mark gets Absent, while teacher-marked sessions stay unrecorded. The worker closes the last 7 days so a day missed while the app was down is still closed. Deleting a slot that has sessions is refused; the admin delete retires the slot so the history stays.

nodes.label: 0007_lecture_sessions
nodes.rationale: Creates lecture_sessions and attendance_excuses and adds nullable attendance.session_id with a RESTRICT foreign key. After upgrading a database that already has attendance rows, backfill sessions before 0008.

nodes.label: Nightly close-day job
nodes.rationale: Inserts not_marked for active slots on a working day of the right weekday inside the current semester when no session row exists. It never creates held rows and never touches a row that exists. Re-running is idempotent. It writes one audit row with the counts and never prints names.

nodes.label: lecture_sessions
nodes.rationale: One row per slot and date: held, cancelled or not_marked. There is no scheduled status, because future lectures have no row until something is known. ON DELETE RESTRICT is on purpose: a slot with sessions cannot be deleted, so the admin single-slot delete must retire it, and a session with marks cannot be deleted. attendance.timetable_id used to cascade, which erased history. session_id stays nullable in 0007 and becomes NOT NULL in 0008 after backfill. marked_by references faculty.id while timetable.faculty_id references faculty.user_id; the app keeps them equal by convention.

nodes.label: Teaching-day scheduling and cancellation
nodes.rationale: The greedy generator and the joint solver place sessions only on teaching days; a week with none fails. Close-day does not open a not_marked session on a non-teaching day, so the nightly digest skips exam and break days. Saving a term cancels unmarked sessions in an exam, break or internship term with cancel_reason calendar; sessions that already have marks are left, and deleting a term does not restore them. Marking a non-teaching day is refused unless that session was already held. Attendance percentages stay unchanged because a cancelled session was already outside the denominator. Holidays in institution_holidays are still removed on top.

nodes.label: Holiday as absence of a session
nodes.norm_label: holiday as absence of a session
nodes.rationale: A holiday is the absence of a session, so it is in no denominator. Close-day creates no row for it. A lecture marked on a holiday, a makeup class, gets a held row and counts. Dated and recurring weekday holidays are honoured through academic_rules.holidays. is_working_day is shared with the generator. institution_holidays had been used by the generator and availability rules, never by attendance.

nodes.label: Device absent fill
nodes.rationale: The old mobile upload wrote a row only for a face-detected student, so everyone else was neither present nor absent. Close-day now writes Absent for roster students a device did not detect on a held mobile session, so a face-marked lecture has a full roster. Teacher-marked sessions are left alone, because a teacher's form says who it covers while a device only says who it saw. The relaxed slot resolver and non-today dates were left in place.

nodes.label: Substitution taught_by
nodes.rationale: taught_by is the approved proxy_log row for that slot and date, otherwise the slot faculty. Marking permission is the slot owner or taught_by for that date. Percentages do not depend on who taught. proxy_assignments has no timetable_id and is not used.

nodes.label: Face consent
nodes.rationale: face_consents holds one row per person per notice version. With FACE_CONSENT_REQUIRED, the default, registration, template upload, distribution and recognition all need an active consent for the current notice version. Withdrawal deletes templates at once and is audited. Raising the notice version makes everyone re-consent; old rows stay as history but no longer count.

nodes.label: Passive liveness and recognition audit
nodes.rationale: A device cannot be fully trusted: a photo held up to the camera will match. Every Present or Late sync event is checked and one face_recognition_audit row is written. Rejection reasons are low confidence below 0.70, low liveness below 0.50 when a score was sent, a duplicate frame hash within 600 seconds, a template older than 730 days, or no consent. A rejected event is not written to attendance_logs. Manual marks and Absent skip the checks. Devices without a liveness model are accepted on confidence alone, so models that produce a score are preferred.

nodes.label: Face template retention
nodes.rationale: The nightly close-day job and flask face purge delete templates after FACE_RETENTION_DAYS when every consent is withdrawn, the user has been inactive, or consent is required and was never given. Withdrawal already deletes immediately; the purge catches older rows. Attendance rows and the recognition audit are kept; only the biometric template goes.

nodes.label: Lecture session codes
nodes.rationale: lecture_sessions.session_code from revision 0007 is now used so a device marks only the lecture the teacher opened. Opening a lecture records it as held and issues an 8-character code valid for 90 minutes. Only the device owner's lectures can be opened from that device. FACE_REQUIRE_SESSION_CODE defaults to false so a college can roll devices out before switching the requirement on. When the flag is off, a code is checked only when one is sent.

nodes.label: 0015_capabilities
nodes.rationale: One row per optional feature. A missing row means the registry default. A missing table means every optional feature is off. Rows are written only from Settings, Capabilities.

nodes.label: Health and incidents
nodes.rationale: /health returns 503 when the database is behind, the worker heartbeat is missing or stale, or free disk is below HEALTH_MIN_FREE_MB. A running export or generation whose heartbeat is older than JOB_STALE_SECONDS is requeued. Maintenance mode leaves the admin panel open for Admin, Super Admin and HOD, including /admin/login, while students, teachers and visitors see the maintenance page. Every log line carries a request id that nginx, the app and the access log share.

nodes.label: Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Everything the product-differentiation roadmap adds is a capability: an optional feature the core never depends on. Sign-in, attendance, timetable generation and reports work with every capability off.

nodes.label: Shared job-claim columns
nodes.rationale: A worker writes its id when it claims a row and refreshes the heartbeat on every progress update. The same locked_by and heartbeat_at columns are on processed_reports, timetable_jobs, notifications and webhook_deliveries, so one restart rule covers exports, generation, mail and webhooks.

nodes.label: Capability fail-closed
nodes.rationale: Missing pieces turn a capability off: no capabilities table, an unknown name, or a lookup error. An install that never visits Settings, Capabilities behaves exactly as before. Registry defaults are on only when on-with-nothing-configured is today's behaviour. Anything that needs a provider, an approval workflow or new data is off by default. Outside an app context, background workers also answer off.

nodes.label: Server flag and tenant switch
nodes.rationale: A capability is on only when both the server flag FEATURE_NAME and the tenant capabilities.enabled row are on. The server flag hides the feature for every tenant. The tenant switch defaults to the registry default when no row has been saved. This is the same shape as NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED plus notification_settings.enabled. The capability is checked after the permission check: capabilities decide whether a feature exists, permissions decide who may use it.

nodes.label: Webhook HMAC signature
nodes.rationale: The endpoint secret is shown once and stored Fernet-encrypted with SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the same key as SMTP settings. Verify by recomputing HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp and raw body, comparing in constant time, and rejecting timestamps older than five minutes. Use X-Timetable-Delivery to de-duplicate, because a retry re-sends the same id.

nodes.label: Webhook outbox
nodes.rationale: Triggers write webhook_deliveries inside the transaction that made the change, so a rolled-back change produces no webhook. Events are attendance.marked, timetable.published and attendance.defaulters, the last of which is the notification trigger. Any non-2xx or a timeout retries with growing delay up to 8 attempts. https is required in production. Hosts that resolve to private, loopback or link-local addresses are refused unless WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE is set, so an endpoint cannot be pointed at the server's own network. WEBHOOKS_ENABLED false stops the worker; triggers queue nothing when there are no endpoints.

nodes.label: Notification dedupe_key
nodes.rationale: dedupe_key is unique. A trigger that fires twice, such as close-day catch-up, a double submit, or an admin re-approving, queues one message, not two. Defaulter mail is once per student per calendar month.

nodes.label: Notification outbox
nodes.rationale: Everything goes through one outbox so a trigger never sends mail from inside a web request and a failed SMTP server never loses a message. The row is inserted on the cursor of the change and commits with it. The worker claims the oldest queued row whose available_at has passed, using the same locked_by and heartbeat_at claim as the other queues. After NOTIFICATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS the row becomes failed and stays visible. When no SMTP account is configured the row stays queued and no attempt is used. NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED false turns the feature off for every tenant. A recipient with no email produces a skipped row so the trigger is still visible.

nodes.label: SMTP account selection
nodes.rationale: Mail prefers the institution account on the settings page. The password is Fernet-encrypted with SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, else FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY, else a key derived from SECRET_KEY. Rotating the key in use makes stored passwords unreadable. Otherwise the server SMTP environment variables are used, the same ones the alert handler uses. The API never returns the password, only has_password.

nodes.label: 0016_timetable_preferences
nodes.rationale: Creates faculty_preferences and timetable_rules. Both are read only when the timetable_preferences capability is on.

nodes.label: 0017_timetable_versions
nodes.rationale: Draft rows carry is_active 0 so readers that filter active rows are unaffected. Null version_id means a row written before versions or while the capability is off. Downgrade turns every draft row into an ordinary retired row.

nodes.label: 0018_bookings
nodes.rationale: A room reserved for an event, exam, maintenance or external use. Only approved rows block a room, and only while the bookings capability is on.

nodes.label: CAPABILITIES registry
nodes.rationale: core.capabilities.CAPABILITIES is the single list: name, title, description, phase, default and a settings schema. The settings page renders from that schema and clean_settings rejects unknown keys. On by default: timetable_preferences, timetable_versions, timetable_grid, calendar_feeds. Off by default: bookings, workload_norms, academic_terms, syllabus, assessments, exams, two_factor, privacy_tools, channels, guardians, attendance_policies.

nodes.label: TIMETABLE.md
nodes.rationale: Generating timetables: the class-by-class generator, the joint CP-SAT solver for shared faculty, electives and lab batches, manual slots, and the clash rules.

nodes.label: bookings capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. Off, room_usage_for_week and booked_room return nothing without touching the table, so the generator, the joint solver and check_slot behave exactly as before. requires_approval defaults to true so requests wait for the room owner's rooms_change_room holders; false approves every clash-free booking at once.

nodes.label: require_capability route guard
nodes.rationale: The guard answers 404 capability_off when the feature is off. GET /api/session carries the effective map, and the UI hides entries with useCapability, but nothing in the UI can switch a feature on: an API behind the guard still answers 404. New tables must not be referenced by a NOT NULL foreign key from the core schema.

nodes.label: timetable_preferences capability
nodes.rationale: On by default once its revision is applied, because on-with-nothing-configured keeps today's behaviour through built-in weights. Off, the solvers use the legacy objective and no preferences, and the rules and preferences routes answer 404.

nodes.label: timetable_versions capability
nodes.rationale: On by default. The job worker opens a draft only when it is on; otherwise generation replaces live rows directly. keep_drafts bounds how many drafts an institution keeps. An operator who wants the old behaviour switches it off or sets FEATURE_TIMETABLE_VERSIONS false.

nodes.label: Room and faculty sharing
nodes.rationale: A shared resource is one row with a policy, never a copy. private is the owning institution, listed adds resource_shares, and organization is every institution of the tenant. Both solvers load rooms through that predicate, so one joint run over two colleges gives each its own pool and a shared elective the intersection. Clash rules do not change: timetable already holds every slot of the tenant, so a shared lab booked by one college is busy for another with no extra ledger. Only the owner edits sharing. Deleting a row other institutions use is refused.

nodes.label: Attendance calculation service
nodes.rationale: Every percentage a screen or export shows comes from services/attendance_calc.py, which loads students, slots, lecture_sessions, marks and excuses and hands them to the pure attendance_calc package. The denominator is held lectures the student was rostered for. A mark the teacher saved always counts even outside that roster. Cancelled lectures, holidays and not_marked lectures are not counted. Late counts as present. An excused absence leaves the denominator. Nothing countable is null, shown as a dash, not 0. Overall and Theory/Practical figures are pooled. ATTENDANCE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT defaults to 75 and can be overridden for one call.

nodes.label: in_roster
nodes.rationale: The one roster rule: same course and class; the slot's division when it has one, otherwise the whole class; an elective requires a chosen subject; when lab batches exist the slot's batch must be in the student's batch ids; enrolment dates bound the day. fetch_lecture_roster is its SQL twin and a test keeps the two in step.

nodes.label: Notification triggers
nodes.rationale: Kinds are lecture_cancelled, proxy_assigned, shift_request, shift_decision, booking_request, booking_decision, not_marked_digest, defaulter and test. Booking triggers follow the master enabled switch and require capability bookings. The not-marked digest and defaulter alerts run after the nightly close-day. Defaulters use ATTENDANCE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT. Each trigger has its own switch; enabled turns the whole institution off.

nodes.label: attendance_calc package
nodes.rationale: Pure Python, no Flask and no SQL, so the figures can be unit-tested with hand-calculated golden values. data_access/attendance_calc.py loads the inputs. services/attendance_calc.py is the only entry point screens, exports and notifications call. Functions are deterministic and take today from the caller. Every number a screen shows comes from StudentSummary. Percentages are Decimal, rounded once, and None when nothing is countable, never 0 and never above 100. Overall and per-component figures are pooled, not the mean of subject percentages.

nodes.label: Excuse rule
nodes.rationale: An excuse excuses an absence, nothing else. Present or Late on an excused date still counts as attended, so a student who came in during sick leave is not penalised. The recommended store is a separate attendance_excuses table with date ranges, and an excused session leaves the denominator rather than counting as present.

nodes.label: Saved-mark roster evidence
nodes.rationale: A mark the teacher saved is evidence the student was in that lecture, so it counts even when the roster rule says otherwise that day. A division transfer, an enrolment date, or an elective choice recorded late never hides saved marks. Only a cancelled session ignores its marks, and cancelling a marked session is refused unless the admin clears them.

nodes.label: Attendance policy defaults
nodes.rationale: Unmarked lectures are excluded from the percentage and shown as a count. Late counts as present. Excused absences leave the denominator. The threshold is an institution setting defaulting to 75. The overall figure is pooled. No data is shown as a dash, never 0. Retired slots' past sessions keep counting. A faculty absence with no approved proxy stays not_marked for a human decision rather than auto-cancelling. Enrolment for phase 1 is students.created_at and, once inactive, students.updated_at, with a proper student_enrolments table left for later so division transfers keep history.

nodes.label: Lab batch roster rule
nodes.rationale: Start from the slot's course and class, narrow to its division, keep elective selections, then keep dated membership in the slot's batch. roster_clauses is the single SQL form, used by the mark screen, history, mobile sync and the mark endpoints. attendance_calc/roster.py applies the same rule in Python. A session before added_at or after ended_at is outside the roster. A saved mark is roster evidence, so marks taken before a move keep counting.

nodes.label: Institution ownership through departments
nodes.rationale: An institution owns courses, subjects, students, allocations, timetable slots, lecture sessions and attendance through the department of the course. High-volume tables never get an institution_id; they inherit through the course. Rooms are anchored directly. Classes, divisions, academic years, semesters, shifts, holidays, roles, branding and notification settings stay organization-wide on purpose, as vocabularies or policy. Per-institution overrides are the obvious next step and are not in this revision.

nodes.label: lab_batch_groups
nodes.rationale: The batches a division is split into, per academic year and optional semester. A null division splits the whole class. A null semester means the same split all year. Batches are re-formed each year. MariaDB treats nulls as distinct in the unique key, so the service also checks for a same-named group before insert or rename. Inactive groups are left out of splits and generation. Capacity is respected by the generator and the member screen.

nodes.label: Tenant organization institution department
nodes.rationale: Tenant is the customer and the isolation boundary. Organization is exactly one row. Institution is the college, school or campus and the accreditation unit. Department remains the HOD scope. A standalone college is one organization and one institution and behaves exactly as before. Nothing here requires the tenant registry; it works in single-database mode too.

nodes.label: Lab batch clash rule
nodes.rationale: A whole-division slot clashes with everything in the division. Two slots of the same batch clash. Slots of different batches do not, so they can run practicals at the same time with different teachers and labs. Faculty and room clashes are unchanged: one person or room, one place. The generator expands each practical into one session per active batch and fills the other batches into the same slot.

nodes.label: Lab batch gap
nodes.rationale: A practical is usually taught to part of a division. course_batches is an intake cohort, not a lab group, and timetable.course_batch_id and students.course_batch_id keep that meaning. Before 0012 no table said which students were in which lab group, so the attendance roster for a lab slot was the whole division and a teacher could mark a student from another batch.

nodes.label: Dated lab batch membership
nodes.rationale: Memberships are dated rather than deleted, so a move from one batch to another keeps history. A student is current in at most one batch per split; set_members enforces that because one unique key cannot. Deleting a group sets timetable.lab_batch_group_id null and turns its slots back into whole-division slots. Attendance is never deleted. Existing rows need no migration because a null batch id stays a whole-division slot.

A booking is one date or a weekly weekday until repeat_until, for an event, exam, maintenance, or an outside party. room_usage_for_week feeds approved bookings to both solvers in the same start/end shape as timetable rows. booked_room lets check_slot refuse a weekly slot that meets a weekly booking (slot_room_booked). A dated booking does not block a weekly slot, because the booking side already refused it if the slot existed first. create and decide refuse a live timetable clash (booking_room_busy) or another approved booking (booking_room_booked) and return free rooms of the same type. Only approved bookings block anything. With requires_approval, default true, a request waits as requested until a rooms_change_room holder of the owning institution decides. A bookings_change or rooms_change_room holder booking a room their own institution owns is approved at once. Sharing follows Institutions through candidate_rooms_clause. Decisions are audited as booking_requested, booking_approved, booking_rejected, and booking_cancelled. Notifications, when on, queue booking_request to approvers and booking_decision to the requester.

nodes.label: Greedy timetable solver
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/generator.py is the default. Classes run one after another. For each class it orders sessions, tries free slots, and picks the first teacher and room that fit. It keeps several candidates and ranks them with the quality model. Fast and dependency-free, and good when classes rarely share staff. A teacher taken by the first class is unavailable to the next, so later classes get the leftovers. With preferences on, candidates are ranked by quality_score minus 0.5 times rule_cost. The slot-by-slot loop is unchanged.

nodes.label: Joint CP-SAT solver
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/joint_solver.py builds one CP-SAT model for every selected class. load_problem turns targets into demands, solve places them, and persist_cohort archives old rows, retires them, and inserts the new timetable with lab_batch_group_id set for batch sessions. It runs for at most TIMETABLE_SOLVER_SECONDS, default 20 from the .env variable, and returns the best feasible solution. Unplaced demands are reported as unassigned slots. When ortools is not installed the job logs a warning and falls back to the greedy generator, so a deployment without the package still generates.

nodes.label: Manual timetable slots
nodes.rationale: services/timetable_slots.add_slot handles POST /api/timetable/slots. It checks holiday, division or batch clash through academic_rules/clashes.cohort_slots_clash, faculty clash and availability, and room clash. Error codes are slot_class_busy, slot_batch_busy, slot_faculty_busy, slot_faculty_unavailable, slot_room_busy, and slot_batch_invalid. DELETE /api/timetable/slots/<id> deletes a slot that has never been used. A slot with attendance or lecture sessions is retired (is_active 0) so marks are kept. Both endpoints need timetable_change.

nodes.label: OR-Tools
nodes.rationale: CP-SAT is built with OR-Tools. The library is the ortools package in requirements.txt. Documentation: https://developers.google.com/optimization.

nodes.label: Timetable quality model
nodes.rationale: timetable_quality_service scores a timetable from 0 to 100 using clash risk, faculty fatigue, room overuse, and load balance. Both solvers are scored the same way so the Generate page can compare them. When max_hours_per_day or max_consecutive_hours is on, the model uses those thresholds for fatigue features.

nodes.label: Soft rule registry
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/rules.py is the single registry. Each rule has a weight from 0 to 20; 0 switches it off. Rules are faculty_preferences, max_hours_per_day, max_consecutive_hours, idle_gaps_students, idle_gaps_faculty, room_changes, spread_subject, lab_blocks_contiguous, no_first_hour_after_evening, lunch_window, prefer_early, and workload_max. default_rules() is the registry default. legacy_rules() is the pre-rules objective. effective_rules(cursor, institution_id, settings) picks one, merges a per-run rules_override, and says whether preferences count. Joint adds every weighted rule to the CP-SAT objective through _soft_terms. Room changes are scored only after room assignment. evaluate() scores any finished timetable. Both solvers return violations, rule_cost, and rule_costs, shown as Why these slots.

nodes.label: Timetable versions service
nodes.rationale: services/timetable/versions.py. publish activates a draft. diff compares two versions or a version against live. Reading needs timetable_versions_view, timetable_change, or timetable_generate. Changing needs timetable_versions_publish or timetable_generate. Versions are scoped to the caller's institutions. Endpoints cover list, detail, diff, publish, rename, and delete. Delete of the live version returns 409 version_published.

nodes.label: Workload service
nodes.rationale: services/workload.py owns workload norms. GET and PUT /api/timetable/workload-norms. PUT is audited as workload_norms_changed. 404 capability_off when the capability is off. 409 rules_table_missing before revision 0016. 400 norms_invalid for hours outside 0-60, min above max, more than 40 designations, or names over 50 characters.

nodes.label: Faculty window preferences
nodes.rationale: faculty_preferences holds one row per teacher window. faculty_id is faculty.user_id. day_of_week 1 is Monday. kind is preferred or avoid. weight is 1 to 5. APIs: GET and PUT /api/faculty/<faculty_id>/preferences, and GET and PUT /api/portal/preferences for the signed-in teacher. A teacher may only reach their own record.

nodes.label: Timetable generate API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/timetable/generate queues the job. GET /api/timetable/jobs/<id> is polled. The body may include solver, rules_override, and an optional draft label.

nodes.label: Lab batches
nodes.rationale: lab_batch_groups: every practical becomes one session per active batch of the division for the academic year that contains the week start date. See DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md.

nodes.label: 0016 timetable preferences
nodes.rationale: Revision 0016_timetable_preferences stores timetable_rules, one JSON document per institution, and faculty_preferences. Workload norms reuse this row under the _workload key.

nodes.label: 0017 timetable versions
nodes.rationale: Revision 0017_timetable_versions. The timetable_versions capability is default on once this revision is applied.

nodes.label: 0018 bookings
nodes.rationale: Revision 0018 adds the bookings table used by the room-booking clash ledger.

nodes.label: Shared solver inputs
nodes.rationale: Both solvers take a scope of one class, one course, or every class; working days and lecture length; subjects split into theory and practical, with electives from student_subject_selections; faculty from faculty_subject_allocations plus faculty_absences and faculty_unavailability; rooms whose room_type contains lab for practicals and the rest for theory, with capacity checked against the group; lab batches; and existing timetable rows outside the job so a teacher or room already booked is not booked again.

nodes.label: timetable_jobs
nodes.rationale: Generation rows are claimed by flask workers run. See RUNBOOK.md. The job result can carry version_id, violations, rule_cost, and rule_costs.

nodes.label: Timetable preferences
nodes.rationale: Capability timetable_preferences. With it off, users do not see the rules below and both solvers keep the historical objective: avoid a subject repeating on a day (weight 10) and prefer earlier slots (1 per slot step). See DESIGN_CAPABILITIES.md.

nodes.label: Timetable versions
nodes.rationale: Capability timetable_versions, default on once revision 0017_timetable_versions is applied. With it off, both solvers replace live rows directly and the version endpoints do not exist. With it on, a job first creates a draft covering every class in the job (timetable_versions and timetable_version_cohorts). Solvers write rows with is_active 0 and timetable.version_id set. The live timetable is untouched, so students, teachers, attendance, exports, the public API, and webhooks keep seeing the current timetable. In a multi-class greedy job, class N treats earlier draft rows as busy and ignores live rows the draft will replace (versions.busy_clause). Drafts beyond keep_drafts, default 10, are pruned oldest first. A draft that placed nothing is dropped. Publish copies active rows to timetable_history, retires them, and activates the version rows, one transaction per request. Classes with no rows are skipped. The timetable.published webhook fires per class with reason published. Rollback is publishing an archived version again. A manual slot added while a version is live is tagged with that version. Only drafts and archived versions can be discarded. Compare pairs slots as unchanged, room_changed, moved, added, or removed, and totals changes per teacher.

nodes.label: Workload norms
nodes.rationale: Capability workload_norms, default off, with enforce soft or hard. A norm is a weekly teaching range in hours, min and max from 0 to 60, per designation, plus a default. Norms are stored in the institution timetable_rules row under the reserved _workload key, so there is no schema beyond revision 0016. rules.load_rules ignores underscore-prefixed keys and save_rules keeps them. limits_for resolves the norm from faculty.designation. weekly_hours sums live timetable rows. assess returns under, ok, over, or no_norm. Soft enforce costs weight times hours over the norm, default weight 6, counting hours inside the run and hours already taught outside it. Hard enforce caps joint placements at the remaining hours and makes greedy treat an over-norm teacher as unavailable. Minimums are never enforced by the solvers; they only flag. Nothing with a minimum is placed as a hard constraint. The faculty-workload report gains designation, norm_min, norm_max, workload_flag, and an outside_norm count. The teacher dashboard shows My workload from GET /api/portal/teacher, null when the capability is off.

nodes.label: DESIGN_CAPABILITIES.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for the capability flags that turn timetable preferences, and the related behavior, on or off.

nodes.label: Generating timetables
nodes.rationale: Generation runs as a background job. The request chooses greedy or joint with solver.

nodes.label: DESIGN_LAB_BATCHES.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for how lab batches split a division's practicals.

nodes.label: Reports documentation
nodes.rationale: docs/REPORTS.md is cited for the faculty-workload report, which gains norm columns while workload norms are on.

nodes.label: RUNBOOK.md
nodes.rationale: Cited for how flask workers run claims timetable_jobs.

nodes.label: Interactive slot check
nodes.rationale: services/timetable_slots.check_slot runs every manual-slot check without writing and returns faculty_id plus errors. add_slot calls it with first_only=True and raises the first error, so the grid predicts exactly what a save would refuse. exclude_id ignores one existing row so a slot can be checked against its new position. POST /api/timetable/check needs timetable_change. rule_cost from slot_cost is present only when the slot is clean and timetable_preferences is on. The Timetable page pre-checks up to 60 cells and shades them green, amber, red, or grey. Confirming a drop does DELETE then POST, so a slot with attendance is retired and the marks stay. Moves go onto an undo stack. GET /api/timetable also serves one teacher or one room. Print hides the controls with print:hidden.

nodes.label: Timetable generation
nodes.rationale: The Generate page queues a job and polls it. Choose joint when several divisions share faculty, electives cross divisions, or lab batches must run in parallel. Choose greedy for a single class or a quick draft.

nodes.label: Joint solver hard rules
nodes.rationale: A demand is placed at most once. A teacher gives one session per slot across cohorts in the job, and none in slots already booked or marked absent or unavailable. A whole-division session excludes everything else for that division. Electives of different subjects may run together. Different lab batches may run together. The same elective subject or the same batch appears at most once per slot. A subject chosen across several divisions is one demand with several cohorts. Room capacity limits practicals to free labs and theory to free rooms. Exact rooms are assigned afterwards by _assign_rooms, largest group first. The same subject occurs at most twice a day per cohort and per batch.

nodes.label: Legacy soft objective
nodes.rationale: legacy_rules() is the pre-rules objective, spread weight 10 and early weight 1, used when timetable_preferences is off.

nodes.label: Parallel lab batches
nodes.rationale: fill_parallel_batches places the other batches of a practical in the same slot with a different teacher and lab when it can, otherwise they take their own slots.
